spans.s:
jaṅgama
(‘that which moves’)
------------------------------------------
In the philosophical literature, the word generally signifies living beings. This whole world comprises two types of things: The sthāvara, and the जङ्गम, the stationary (non-moving, lifeless, material objects) and the moving (living beings).
In the Vīraśaiva or लिङ्गायत सेच्त् of शैविस्म्, the word has a special signi-ficance. It represents a saint, a man of realisation who is ‘dynamic knowledge’ or ‘personification of knowledge, who is moving, who is living’.
The ‘jaṅgama’ is the third ‘āvaraṇa’ (shield of protection) out of the eight, specified in this sect.
A vīraśaiva (follower of वीरशैविस्म्) is ordained to honor a जङ्गम even as he honours his गुरु (spiritual teacher) and the लिङ्ग (emblem of शिव given to him at the time of his initiation).
See also ŚAIVISM.
